questions.q: After StyleGAN's AdaIN, what are the mean and standard deviation of feature map i?
options: The style's y_b,i and y_s,i, whatever the input had
The input's own mean and standard deviation, multiplied by (1 + y_s,i)
Zero and one
Those of the learned constant input
questions.answer: The style's y_b,i and y_s,i, whatever the input had
questions.why: AdaIN(x_i, y) = y_s,i (x_i − μ(x_i)) / σ(x_i) + y_b,i. In the lab a map with mean 40.136 and standard deviation 0.950 comes out with mean 4.000 and standard deviation 3.000, the style's values.

questions.q: In the lab two inputs have the same pattern and differ only by a per-channel scale and offset. What happens?
options: AdaIN gives the same output for both, shift + x(1 + scale) does not
Both give the same output
Neither gives the same output
Only shift + x(1 + scale) gives the same output
questions.answer: AdaIN gives the same output for both, shift + x(1 + scale) does not
questions.why: The largest output difference is 3.6e-15 for AdaIN, which normalises the statistics away, and 42.1 for shift + x(1 + scale), which keeps them.

questions.q: What does StyleGAN2 blame for the water-droplet artifacts, and what does it do instead?
options: AdaIN's separate normalisation of each feature map; it modulates and then demodulates the convolution weights
The mapping network; it removes the mapping network
The learned constant input; it feeds the latent in at the first layer
The discriminator; it trains a larger one
questions.answer: AdaIN's separate normalisation of each feature map; it modulates and then demodulates the convolution weights
questions.why: The paper pinpoints AdaIN and supports the hypothesis by showing the artifacts vanish when normalisation is removed. Equations 1 to 3 scale the weights by the style and then divide by their L2 norm.

questions.q: Why does demodulation give output standard deviations of 0.661 to 1.326 for blurred inputs in the lab, but 1.000 to 1.003 for independent ones?
options: It assumes independent unit-variance inputs, and blurred inputs are correlated
The weights were random in one case and fixed in the other
Blurring changes the number of channels
The style entries were larger for blurred inputs
questions.answer: It assumes independent unit-variance inputs, and blurred inputs are correlated
questions.why: The formula for the output standard deviation is derived for independent inputs. StyleGAN2 calls demodulation weaker than instance normalisation because it rests on statistical assumptions rather than on the actual feature maps.

questions.q: Where does the (1 + scale) pattern appear in ComfyUI's source?
options: In modulate() in mmdit.py and in the use_scale_shift_norm path of the U-Net ResBlock
Only inside StyleGAN checkpoints that ComfyUI loads
In the tokenizer's merge table
In the VAE's tiling code
questions.answer: In modulate() in mmdit.py and in the use_scale_shift_norm path of the U-Net ResBlock
questions.why: modulate returns shift + x(1 + scale), and ResBlock multiplies by (1 + scale) and adds shift when use_scale_shift_norm is set. ComfyUI has no StyleGAN generator; model_animate.py only borrows some StyleGAN2 layers.

questions.q: What does Apply Style Model do to the conditioning in ComfyUI?
options: Adds the reference's tokens to the conditioning, so the prompt tensor gets longer
Runs AdaIN on the feature maps
Loads a StyleGAN generator
Scales the VAE's latent
questions.answer: Adds the reference's tokens to the conditioning, so the prompt tensor gets longer
questions.why: StyleModelApply joins the style output on to the conditioning. The word style there has nothing to do with StyleGAN's mechanism.
